misconception_description: Student believes that colons (:) are used for variable assignment.

solutions.generated_code:
program CekTandaBerlawanan
kamus
  a, b : integer
  hasil : boolean
algoritma
  input(a, b)
  hasil : (a < 0 and b > 0) or (a > 0 and b < 0)
  output(hasil)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student uses `:` instead of `=` to assign the result of the comparison to the variable `result`. While this is syntactically valid Python (it creates a type annotation), it doesn't actually assign the value to `result`. When the function tries to return `result`, it will raise a NameError since `result` was never actually assigned a value - it was only annotated. The student believes this is the correct way to assign values to variables and expects the code to work perfectly.
